key_insight: CG-OMatG combines an equivariant Riemannian flow model with reinforcement learning to generate molecular crystal structures by predicting rigid-molecule centroids, orientations, and lattice parameters in a hierarchical coarse-grained representation.
engineering_relevance: The approach could accelerate polymorph screening and organic solid-state materials discovery by proposing plausible low-energy crystal packings before expensive experimental or simulation-based validation.
method: Treats molecules as rigid bodies and uses inter- and intra-molecular message passing to build a geometric packing representation.
Learns a coarse-grained generative model on the Riemannian manifold of crystal structure variables.
Fine-tunes the generator with policy-gradient reinforcement learning to bias samples toward low-energy candidates.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on subsets of OMC25 and CSD and evaluated on the CSP blind test benchmark using COMPACK packing-similarity against experimentally determined crystals.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the training crystal datasets, and rigid-body coarse graining may miss important intra-molecular flexibility effects in some systems.
paper_title: Riemannian Flow Models with Reinforcement Learning for Molecular Crystal Structure Prediction
